homonyms.basis: The census record carries no disambiguation field; its negative tags keep the monitor apart from the IPTC's 2019 social-media test and from a C2PA verifier (PE-13, PE-14). No card is a homonym. Wikipedia's only article under the name is 'MetaWatch', a discontinued smartwatch brand of Meta Watch Ltd. (Strata and Frame, 2012; B7-MetaWatch-homonym.wiki), and the web searches for the LinkedIn card returned the same smartwatch (makezine, techcrunch, ablogtowatch): a distinct entity, never a sense of the name.

captures.description: IPTC METAWATCH, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a free and open public monitoring tool that tracks how news publishers handle photo metadata.' Four features: monthly crawls, over 500 publishers in 122 countries, the fields tracked (credits, captions, copyright notices, Exif, IPTC and XMP), a per-field breakdown. Six cards, five the IPTC's (the announcement of 5 October 2026, the overview, the per-field page, a September events post, the photo-metadata archive), one LinkedIn post by Paul Melcher dated 14 September 2026.

atoms.evidence: Checks whether crucial embedded details—such as credits, captions, copyright notices, Exif data, and IPTC/XMP photo metadata—are preserved or stripped when images are published online.
a free and open public monitoring tool
Monthly Checks: Automatically crawls and analyzes news websites every month to see if embedded metadata survives publication.
